title: Monetary Authority Of Singapore Scheme Backs Standard Chartered's Quantum Computing Research
excerpt: Standard Chartered expands its Quantum Computing research program with backing from the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s FSTI scheme.
content:
Standard Chartered achieved an 18-fold reduction in trainable parameters when fine-tuning large language models using quantum-inspired adapters, a result stemming from a research program backed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s FSTI Quantum Technology scheme. The bank’s work, focused on applications like credit risk assessment and volatile market forecasting, demonstrates a practical approach to quantum computing beyond typical optimization problems.

Across evaluated scenarios, combining conventional forecasting models with quantum techniques improved predictive performance while using 28% fewer parameters. Elena Strbac, Global Head, Data Science & Innovation, Corporate & Investment Bank at Standard Chartered, said: “The biggest risk with quantum is waiting for certainty before getting started.”

This improvement, stemming from the bank’s research program, highlights a practical application of quantum techniques beyond theoretical possibilities and into areas of immediate financial relevance. The program’s initial year focused on three key areas: language modeling, time-series forecasting and financial derivative pricing, all with the aim of identifying where quantum methods could offer a distinct advantage. This backing allowed the bank to investigate quantum and quantum-inspired solutions for computationally intensive problems within finance, building expertise and partnerships essential for future adoption.

This parameter reduction is significant, as it suggests the potential for leaner, more efficient forecasting systems. The program’s work on pricing complex financial derivatives revealed that quantum algorithms achieved comparable accuracy to existing methods, but with up to 18 times fewer computational iterations. This efficiency gain is particularly valuable in risk management and investment strategies, where rapid and accurate pricing is essential.

This includes a deliberate focus on identifying specific problems where quantum techniques offer a clear advantage over classical approaches, rather than pursuing quantum solutions indiscriminately. The research focuses on understanding the practical limitations and requirements for integrating quantum computing into real-world financial applications. The program’s emphasis on selective experimentation and building internal expertise positions Standard Chartered to benefit from quantum advancements as they mature, ensuring the bank is well-prepared to use the technology when it delivers tangible benefits.
